claves: Hongo unicelular. Se parece a los cocos, pero es eucariota (se ven los núcleos) y mucho más grande. Causa infecciones vaginales por levaduras y el muguet (algodoncillo) oral, común en bebés.

imagen.autor: modification of work by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
imagen.descripcionOriginal: Candida albicans is a unicellular fungus, or yeast. It is the causative agent of vaginal yeast infections as well as oral thrush, a yeast infection of the mouth that commonly afflicts infants. C. albicans has a morphology similar to that of coccus bacteria; however, yeast is a eukaryotic organism (note the nuclei) and is much larger. (credit: modification of work by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)
